clue.text: One jerk in a VW is someone like Cameron?

indicators.note: in tells us the first two pieces sit inside the car's name

parts.note: the Polo is a Volkswagen model
one is the Roman numeral I
a tic is an involuntary jerk or twitch

explanation.surface: A fool sitting in a Volkswagen is compared to David Cameron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerk' reads as an insult but is a twitch. David Cameron was British Prime Minister from 2010 to 2016; the question mark shows he is just an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Cameron is an example of a professional politician, which is what this informal word names.

clue.text: Get hairy Anne her clippers and shaving device

indicators.note: hairy can mean wild or alarming, so the following letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone fetches clippers and a razor for a hirsute woman called Anne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hairy' signals the anagram of ANNE HER CLIPPERS; 'Get' just tells the solver to do it. The definition is playful: the thing shaves wood from a writing tool, not hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical description: this desk tool takes shavings off the wood around a lead.

clue.text: Mouth on fish reveals oily substance

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the first piece above the second

parts.note: lip and mouth are both slang for cheeky talk
the id (also ide) is a freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: Looking at a fish's mouth shows something greasy.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the chemical class that includes fats and oils, hence an example-by-category match.

clue.text: Amazing Irish stouts — Dublin has many

indicators.note: amazing suggests bewildering, so the letters that follow are put in a confused order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Dublin is full of wonderful dark Irish beers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amazing' signals an anagram of IR (Irish) plus STOUTS. The definition is the loose closing remark, not the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Visitors on holiday flock to the Irish capital, so the city indeed has plenty of these sightseers.

clue.text: What mountaineer does with cold arm or leg

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
an arm or a leg is a limb

explanation.surface: A mountaineer carries on despite a freezing arm or leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascending rock faces is the activity that describes a mountaineer's sport.

clue.text: Man is after beer, initially — then a dance

indicators.note: after says that the word is follows the letter taken from beer
initially asks for just the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: taken as written
a hop is an informal dance, as in a school hop

explanation.surface: A chap wants a pint first and a boogie afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a chess piece, not a fellow. 'initially' takes B from beer, 'after' puts IS behind it, and 'then' adds the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A chessman is called a man, and this piece is one example.

clue.text: Quite sick, eg

parts.note: sick means ill
say can stand for 'for example', as eg does

explanation.surface: Somebody is described as fairly unwell, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite' as an interjection of hearty agreement is the definition; with the apostrophe the answer is the same exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are spoken exclamations of emphatic agreement, so they are idiomatic synonyms.

clue.text: Controversial issue incensed king Edward ?

parts.note: hot can mean angry, as in hot under the collar
King Edward is a British variety of spud

explanation.surface: A divisive matter infuriated King Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: The King Edward is a popular British variety of the vegetable, not a monarch; the question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a touchy matter nobody wants to handle.

clue.text: Stars on island take small boat without a bite to eat

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the constellation above the pieces that follow

parts.note: the Plough is the British name for the Big Dipper group of stars
the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes

indicators.note: without tells us the boat loses the letter named straight afterwards

parts.note: a launch is a motor boat
the letter to be removed

explanation.surface: Celebrities on an island set off in a little boat with no food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes A from LAUNCH. The answer is a British pub meal of bread, cheese and pickle.
explanation.definitionFit: This pub meal of bread and cheese is an example of a light snack.

clue.text: Simple arrangement around gold appeals

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters go round the heraldic metal
arrangement tells us the letters of the word before it are put in a new order

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: A plain setting round a gold piece is attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appeals' wants to mean attracts; it is the verb for begs. 'arrangement' yields IMPLES, which 'around' then splits about the heraldic gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs for begging earnestly, so they are synonyms in the third person.

clue.text: Change menu and put in scarce chemical

indicators.note: change is an instruction to alter the order of the letters that follow

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook alters the menu and adds a rare chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' signals the anagram of MENU, PUT and IN; 'and' only joins the fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: This radioactive element, number 93, occurs naturally only in trace amounts, so it is rare.

clue.text: Toilet's dry inside but you're chancing your luck here!

indicators.note: inside puts the abbreviation for dry within the word for toilet

parts.note: loo is the everyday British word for a toilet
TT is short for teetotal, dry in the sense of not drinking

explanation.surface: The lavatory is dry inside, but using it is still a gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry' means teetotal, abbreviated TT, and 'inside' places it in LOO, the British word for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a numbers game of chance, a place where players try their fortune.

clue.text: Lemur hiding in spin drier

indicators.note: hiding in says the creature lurks within the letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A lemur has concealed itself in a laundry machine.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the largest living species of Madagascan primate in that family, an example.

clue.text: In America check pipe going round a river's offshoot

indicators.note: going round says the two joined pieces enclose the letter that follows

parts.note: in the US a restaurant bill is called the check
a bong is a water pipe for smoking

explanation.surface: In the US, inspectors examine a pipeline that skirts a branch of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'check' looks like a verb, but with 'In America' it is the US word for what a diner pays; 'going round' makes the two nouns together enclose the article.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian word names a backwater or branch left by a stream.

clue.text: Love the knitted sweater being worn

indicators.note: being worn says the word the is clothed by the reworked jumper letters
knitted suggests the letters of the next word are worked into a new pattern

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone adores the hand-knitted jumper a person has on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' looks like a verb but is a term of endearment. 'knitted' yields SWEEART, and 'being worn' means that garment clothes the article.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are affectionate terms of address for a darling.

clue.text: Journo without rum is no longer friendly

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside puts the journalist around the next word

parts.note: ed is short for editor, a journalist
rum is British slang for odd or peculiar

explanation.surface: A reporter deprived of his spirits has turned hostile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking, so ED surrounds STRANGE. 'rum' is the British adjective for odd, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes people alienated from one another after having been close.

clue.text: Inscription on a sort of pie chart

indicators.note: sort as an instruction means put the neighbouring letters in order

parts.note: a graph is a chart of data

explanation.surface: Wording is engraved on a kind of circular diagram.
explanation.walkthrough: The familiar phrase 'pie chart' must be split: 'sort of' reorders only the first word to EPI, while the second is swapped for a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A motto carved on a monument or quoted at the head of a book is exactly this.

clue.text: After fight maiden is easily aroused

indicators.note: after puts the cricket abbreviation behind the word for a fight

parts.note: a war is a fight on a large scale
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Following a brawl, a young woman is quick to get excited.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes an ardent, passionate temperament, a synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Another aspect of someone revealed by jerk on sky?

indicators.note: in a down clue, on sets the first word above the second

parts.note: to flip is to toss with a jerk
side is dated British slang for a television channel, and Sky is one

explanation.surface: A fool appearing on satellite TV shows a different facet of a person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side' was British slang for a TV channel; Sky is a British satellite broadcaster, the question mark marking it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the reverse or less familiar face of a person or thing.

clue.text: Laws passed when outside court

indicators.note: outside says the word for when goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
Ct is the abbreviation for court in addresses

explanation.surface: Legislation went through while people stood beyond the courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Statutes that parliament has approved are called this.

clue.text: Model left school and went into movie industry

indicators.note: to model is to shape or mould, so the letters after it are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fashion model quit her education and joined the film business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' is an instruction to reshape L, S and WENT INTO; 'and' only joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A nickname for Hollywood, and so for the American film business.

clue.text: It can shock and ruin the reception still

definitions.text: It can shock and ruin the reception
definitions.meaning: electrical charge that gives a jolt, and crackling interference on a radio

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a build-up of electric charge or radio crackle and being motionless.

clue.text: Rendered incapable

definitions.meaning: to render a wall is to coat it with a first layer of cement or similar
incapable is a euphemism for very drunk, as in drunk and incapable

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both a wall given its coating and a person helplessly intoxicated.

clue.text: Start to gasp in terrible air?

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the word for terrible

parts.note: dire means dreadful

indicators.note: start to asks for only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone begins choking in awful polluted atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air' is a tune, not what we breathe. 'Start to' takes G from gasp and 'in' puts it within DIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mournful funeral song is one example of a tune, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Sell drugs on the radio related to feet

indicators.note: on the radio means the phrase is heard, not seen in writing

parts.note: to peddle is to deal in drugs

explanation.surface: A broadcast about dealing narcotics has something to do with feet.
explanation.definitionFit: As an anatomical adjective it means of the foot.

clue.text: Silent old movie

parts.note: dumb means unable or unwilling to speak

explanation.surface: A film from the days before talkies.
explanation.definitionFit: Disney's 1941 animated film about a flying elephant is an example.

clue.text: Illumination needed now towards end of event

parts.note: nigh means near, as towards does in 'towards evening'

indicators.note: end of asks for the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: As the occasion draws to a close, lamps are required.
explanation.definitionFit: A teasing description: the dark hours are when lamps are required.

clue.text: When away simmer a lot of stew without fruit

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside puts the shortened pool around the other piece
a lot of means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a stew is a pond for keeping fish

indicators.note: away suggests out of place, so the letters of the next word are disturbed

explanation.surface: While you are out, leave a big pot of casserole bubbling with no fruit in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' is no casserole but an old word for a fish pool, cut short by 'a lot of'. 'When away' yields ERSIMM, and 'without' means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange-red edible produce of a tree, also called sharon, is an example.

clue.text: Run and develop diet

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
to educe is to draw out or develop

explanation.surface: Go jogging and work out an eating plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diet' is a verb here, meaning to slim.
explanation.definitionFit: Used intransitively it means to slim, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Giant pair of flying insects hard to take in

indicators.note: to take in says the two creatures together admit the abbreviation before them

parts.note: a bee is one winged insect
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
a moth is another winged insect

explanation.surface: A huge couple of winged bugs are difficult to believe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pair of' promises two of one creature, but the setter means two different winged insects side by side, which 'to take in' opens for the pencil abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical monster's name is used for anything enormous.
